checked_obligation: Verify that the assumption ord_p(-a)=(p-1)/2 implies ord_p(a)=p-1.

counterexample.witness: Take p=7 and a=5. Then -a\equiv2\pmod7 has order 3=(p-1)/2, but a^3=125\equiv1\pmod2.

reason: The conclusion is true, but the written argument contains false assertions: it claims a^{(p-1)/2}\not\equiv1\pmod 2, although -1\equiv1\pmod2, and later invokes ord_p(-a)=p-1, contradicting the converse assumption. The prime-divisor criterion is therefore not justified as written.
unresolved_conditions: Replace the modulus 2 by p when proving a^{(p-1)/2}\not\equiv1.
For each odd prime p_i dividing p-1, justify the noncongruence using ord_p(-a)=(p-1)/2 and (p-1)/2\nmid(p-1)/p_i, rather than the false claim that ord_p(-a)=p-1.
